premise_the_numbers_are_conditional_on: The utility functional credits min(kv, remaining) for hiding swap-out under a running tool call, and charges the differential restore only on short calls. That is coherent ONLY under forced eviction: it assumes a long call would have been evicted anyway, so its restore cancels across arms, while a short call's eviction was created by the policy. With no memory pressure the optimal policy is never swap and every arm scores 0. CLOSED-QUESTIONS.md states Fresh-277 cannot measure contention, so this lane is scored under a premise its corpus cannot exhibit. Between-arm comparisons remain valid; the absolute seconds are hidden-swap-ms under an assumed forced-eviction regime, NOT wall clock saved.

why.subgroup_purity_achieved: the stump isolated a subgroup above the frozen 48.5% bar (fired P(long)=69.0% at kv=3500, 66.7% at kv=5000), so the CPU trajectory carries real signal.
why.volume_collapses: it fires on 29 of 1794 survivors at kv=3500 and 3 of 1794 at kv=5000, approaching never-fire, which is deadline_only.
why.frozen_bar_was_mis_specified: rho/(1+rho) assumes a long call hides the full K. Firing at t hides only min(K, latency-t), so a call ending at 4 s fired at 1 s with K=3500 hides 2.6 s and still eats 0.9 s exposure. A 69%-pure subgroup can be net-negative. The correct condition involves the remaining-time distribution given long, not P(long) alone. Recorded, not repaired.
why.elapsed_only_corroborates: firing on every survivor at 1 s loses 2574 s and 6178 s despite survivor P(long)=48.4% at kv=3500, right at the nominal bar.

correction.landmark_prose: the frozen text called t=1000 ms 'the first point with two complete 500 ms windows'. Windows END at 0.501/1.002/1.504 s, so 1000 ms admits exactly ONE complete window. Landmark and pre-recorded population (1794 survivors, P(long) 48.4%/37.4%) unchanged; only the prose was wrong.
